_about: Project playbooks: learnings from projects clubs have run. The three entries below are SAMPLE content to show the format. Replace them with real playbooks and set "sample" to false. photos is optional: a list of { "src": "assets/img/playbooks/file.jpg", "alt": "what the photo shows" }.

items.objective: Clear plastic waste from a 1 km stretch of beach and teach visitors how to segregate waste.
whatWasDone: Took written permission from the local authority two weeks before the drive.
Split 40 volunteers into 5 teams, each with a team lead and a stretch of beach.
Weighed each bag at a collection point and handed dry waste to a recycler.
Ran a 20-minute segregation talk for families on the beach.

budget.notes: Gloves, bags, water, snacks, and transport for the waste.

whatWorked: Team leads with one clear stretch each: no area was missed and no team waited.
Weighing bags on the spot gave us impact numbers for the report the same day.
Starting at 7 am, before the heat and the crowd.
doDifferently: Check the tide table. High tide covered part of our stretch at 9 am.
Book the waste pickup vehicle in writing. Ours came two hours late.
Carry more water. We ran out by 9:30 am.
tips: Take a before and after photo of the same spot for social media.
Keep one volunteer only for photos and impact data.

items.objective: Collect 100 units of blood for a partner blood bank ahead of the holiday shortage.
whatWasDone: Partnered with a licensed blood bank that brought its own doctors and equipment.
Ran a two-week registration drive in colleges and housing societies.
Set up a waiting area with snacks and a volunteer desk for first-time donors.

budget.notes: Refreshments, banners, donor certificates, and volunteer T-shirts.

whatWorked: Online registration with time slots. The queue never got long.
A short WhatsApp reminder the evening before cut no-shows.
Certificates handed over on the spot made donors share photos.
doDifferently: Explain the eligibility rules in the registration form. Many people were turned away for low haemoglobin or recent travel.
Plan for more volunteers at the snack table after donation.
tips: Confirm the blood bank's licence and the date in writing.
Thank each donor on the club page only with their consent.

items.objective: Teach college students how to budget, save, and stay safe from online payment fraud.
whatWasDone: Invited a bank officer as the facilitator and briefed them on the audience.
Built a budgeting game with play money for groups of five.
Ended with a quiz and a take-home one-page budget sheet.
whatWorked: The budgeting game. Students stayed after the session to finish it.
A quiz before and after gave clear numbers for the report.
doDifferently: Keep the talk part under 30 minutes.
Close registrations two days earlier so we can print the right number of kits.
tips: Ask the facilitator for a short bio in advance for the emcee.
Use the AI Shortcut to write the invitation and the thank-you note.
